transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Well, I'm here because... I guess things have just gotten a little out of hand lately. I’ve been taking on far more projects and workshops than I can realistically manage right now. Plus, I started all these studio improvements—I decided to completely redo the lighting and tear up the flooring in my workspace because the natural light was just hitting the canvases all wrong in the late afternoons. It actually reminded me of this graduate seminar I took in Florence years ago, where the professor was absolutely obsessed with chiaroscuro. He used to make us paint in near darkness. He had this little fawn pug that would sleep under the easels... such a sweet dog, it snored so loudly. I've always wanted a pug, or maybe a French bulldog, but they have so many breathing issues, you know? 

But, um, anyway... between the renovations and scheduling all these new client calls back-to-back, I'm just buried. Now the deadlines and the mortgage are really starting to close in on me, and I just... I don't really know how I'm going to get it all done.
Have you noticed yourself feeling more energetic or needing less sleep lately, especially when you’ve been starting all these new projects?

Energetic? Oh, absolutely. It’s like... I’ve had this humming current in me from morning on. Sitting quietly has felt almost impossible lately. So I just keep moving, you know? I’ve been constantly rearranging the studio, drafting all those new proposals, emailing people, and just fussing with my supplies. 

Actually, speaking of supplies, I just got this massive shipment of ultramarine and cadmium oils from a boutique maker in Belgium. He hand-mixes the pigments with walnut oil instead of linseed. Linseed yellows so terribly over time. If you look at some of the late nineteenth-century portraits in the museum, you can see how the linseed just completely ruined the complexions of the subjects. They all look like they have jaundice! My aunt had jaundice when I was a teenager, and her skin was exactly that color. She had to stay in the hospital for a week, and the food there was absolutely dreadful. Just green Jello every single day, and I remember the nurses wore those very stiff, white caps that you just don't see anymore. 

But, um... anyway, yes, with that humming feeling, I just couldn't sit still, so I kept drafting things and moving my canvases around.
Have you noticed your mood being unusually high, elevated, or irritable during this time, different from your usual self?

High? Oh, yes, absolutely. Most days I’ve just felt unusually buoyant... really lit up, you know? It felt like everything in the studio and my garden were finally, perfectly clicking into place. 

The garden, actually, has been just spectacular lately. I finally got the soil acidity right for my hydrangeas. If the soil is too alkaline, they turn pink, and pink just clashes terribly with the red brick on the side of the house. My neighbor, Susan, she has pink ones, and she puts out these awful plastic flamingos next to them. I just can't fathom buying plastic yard art when there are so many beautiful, hand-thrown ceramic pieces out there. I actually took a wheel-throwing class back in the late nineties, and the clay just destroys your cuticles, but it's so therapeutic. 

But, oh, right, my mood. Yes, very high-spirited. But also... yes, irritable. Very much so. If anyone dared to question my plans or, heaven forbid, asked me about invoices, I would just snap so sharply at them. My accountant called asking about some outstanding invoices and receipts, and I just completely bit his head off. And honestly, they print receipts on that terrible thermal paper now anyway. It fades after a few months, so what's the point of even filing them? Plus, I read it's covered in BPA or something toxic, so you really shouldn't even touch it with your bare hands. 

But, um... yes, I definitely felt very elevated, but I'd snap at people in a heartbeat if they got in my way.
Can you describe how long this unusually elevated or irritable mood has been going on, and whether it’s been present most of the day, nearly every day, during this time?

Well, it's been... I'd say about three months now. It all really started right around the time I took on the mortgage for the new cottage-studio. The cottage is just darling, really, it has these original leaded glass windows from the 1920s. Though, honestly, they are incredibly drafty. I had to buy this heavy velvet curtain to hang over the door just to keep the chill out. Velvet is so difficult to clean, though. You can't just toss it in the wash, you have to take it to a specialist dry cleaner, and the one down the street from me just closed. The owner retired and moved to Boca Raton. I can't imagine living in Florida, the humidity would just ruin my canvases, and frizzy hair is just a nightmare to deal with. 

But, um, yes, to answer your question... it's been pretty much all day, every day for the last three months, ever since I signed the papers for that cottage.
Have you experienced a significant decrease in the amount of sleep you need, where you felt rested with much less sleep than usual?

Sleep? Um, I haven't really noticed a decrease in how much sleep I need, to be honest. I mean, I'm not really sure what you mean by needing less sleep and feeling rested. I think I've just been sleeping normally. 

Although, my mattress has been giving me the worst backaches lately. It's one of those memory foam ones, and they say it's supposed to contour to your body, but honestly, it just feels like sinking into wet cement. I tried putting a mattress topper on it—one of those down alternative ones because real down makes me sneeze uncontrollably. I actually found out I was allergic to down when I stayed at this bed and breakfast in Vermont. The whole room was just covered in feathers, even the decorative pillows. The owner was this lovely woman who made her own maple syrup, but the syrup was so thin, not at all like the thick kind you buy at the store. I think she watered it down. 

But anyway, no, I haven't really noticed any changes with my sleep.
Have you been engaging in more goal-directed activities than usual, like starting new projects or taking on more tasks, even when they aren't necessary or have questionable benefits?

Oh, absolutely. Actually, that's really the main reason I came in to see you. I’ve been taking on far, far more projects than I can realistically manage. I started scheduling all these new workshops, doing massive studio improvements, fielding endless client calls... 

I decided I absolutely had to rip out the studio flooring myself to put in reclaimed barn wood because the old laminate was just so uninspiring. Reclaimed wood has so much history to it, you know? Though, I bought it from this salvage yard out in the county, and the man who ran it had the most bizarre accent. I think it was maybe Dutch? I went to Amsterdam once right after grad school, and the bicycles there are just an absolute menace. People think it's so quaint, but you're constantly dodging them on the street. And the cheese is good, but honestly, I prefer a really sharp Wisconsin cheddar. My uncle used to send us a block every Christmas, wrapped in that red wax. Peeling the wax off is so satisfying, almost like popping bubble wrap. 

But anyway, yes, the studio improvements, and the client calls. I was booking commission after commission. One client wanted a massive triptych for her dining room, but she insisted it be entirely in shades of chartreuse. Chartreuse is such a difficult color to live with, it reflects terribly onto the food. Who wants to eat a roast chicken in a neon green room? It makes everyone look seasick. I told her to go with a warm ochre, but people just don't listen to professionals anymore. They see one picture on Pinterest and suddenly they think they have a fine arts degree. 

But, um... what was I saying? Right, the projects. I just took on so many of them, and now all the deadlines are hitting at once, and with that new cottage mortgage I mentioned earlier... it's all just really starting to close in on me.
